senses.gloss:
ucchiṣṭa
(‘the leftover’)
------------------------------------------
In the most general sense, it means anything left over after a rite or action. For instance, oblatory materials like ghee, leftover after a होम or a यज्ञ (sacrifice) is उच्छिष्ट.
However it is more commonly used with regard to the ड़ोओद् leftover in the plate after a person has eaten.
Though some धर्मशास्त्रस् like the Baudhāyana-dharmasūtras (1.2.34, 37) allow a disciple to eat the उच्छिष्ट of his गुरु, it was discouraged later.

Ucchiṣṭa-gaṇapati
------------------------------------------
This is one of the thirty-two major forms of गणपति. It is a form mentioned in the तन्त्रस् and worshipped for magical ends.
The expression ‘ucchiṣṭa’ (‘leftover’) here signifies ब्रह्मन्, because that alone—or He alone—remains even after the dissolution of the whole world.
गणपति.jpg" src="http://eoh.rkmathbangalore.org/public/images/thumbs/Ucchi%E1%B9%A3%E1%B9%ADa-ga%E1%B9%87apati.jpg" alt="Ucchiṣṭa-गणपति">It may also mean ‘unclean’. उच्छिष्ट-गणपति is absolute and mighty but unclean or indecent in appearance. He is capable of granting the desires of his votaries even though they too may be unclean!
His images may have six arms or four. The things shown in his hands include lotus, pomegranate, lute, bunch of paddy grains, rosary, bow, arrow, noose, goad, sweetmeat, bowl and broken tusk. He is usually shown with his शक्ति (consort) in an amorous pose.
See also GAṆAPATI.
